correctness.rationale: Reconstructed F_r on the zero-sum unit sphere and its exact Löwner-radius minimizer characterization from irreducible permutation symmetry. The zero-sum quartic constrained maximization has only signed one-outlier nondegenerate maxima: stationarity produces a cubic with at most three roots; repeated outer root gives a positive tangent second variation, and the only 3-root candidate is two-sparse and a saddle for N>=4. At the one-outlier orbit, the constrained quartic Hessian is -4(N-3)/(N-1) times the tangent norm squared. Uniform C2 Taylor perturbation of F_r=r^2/2-r^4 Q/12+O(r^6) and exact orbit stationarity give small-r minimizers. For r large, sum |u_i|>=sqrt(2) with equality only signed two-sparse points; positive/negative mass deficits and |t|-log2<=log cosh t<=|t| imply the stated quantitative distance. The small and large contact orbits are disjoint. Finite random tests do not establish the global quartic critical-point lemma.
